name: China economy
summary: China's October output rose 4.8% and retail sales slowed; new home prices fell 2.4% on a year, the 40th annual fall
state: Statistics bureau data of 16 Nov showed October industrial output up 4.8% on a year, a three-month low, with retail sales growth slowing and investment missing estimates (NBS; Trading Economics). New home prices in 70 cities fell 2.4% on a year in October, the 40th straight annual decline but the slowest since November 2025 (Trading Economics). Searches on 20 Nov found no new developer default wave, financial contagion or tightened capital controls, so Normal holds with momentum weakening.
for_you: Slower Chinese spending tends to weigh on exporters of commodities and consumer goods to China, and on firms with large sales there.
rubric_hit: Growth near target, no contagion or new developer defaults: Normal; weak retail and investment noted

sources.title: National Bureau of Statistics of China — National economy generally stable in October

why: China is the world's factory and the biggest marginal buyer of commodities; a hard landing would ripple through every supply chain.
drivers: Property sector, local-government debt, exports and tariffs, deflation, stimulus.

rubric.alert: Hard landing (growth < 3%), financial contagion, or capital controls tightened sharply.
rubric.watch: Deflation, renewed property-developer defaults, or growth clearly below target.
rubric.normal: Growth near official target, stable property sales, no financial contagion.
